stem:
Sia multiplies $\dfrac{2}{3}$ by $\dfrac{5}{7}$.

Which claim about the product is correct?

options.text: Call the answer fraction factors, and stop with no product written.
Writing $\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{5}{7}$ is what creates the order of the factors.
$\dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{5}{7} = \dfrac{5}{7} \times \dfrac{2}{3}$, because the order of the factors does not change the product.
The product equals $\dfrac{2}{3}$, because $2$ and $3$ are the first numerals printed.

teacher.key_rationale: Multiplication of fractions is commutative, so swapping the factors leaves the product unchanged. Naming fraction factors alone substitutes a label. Saying the product writing creates the order reverses the relation. Grabbing the first printed numerals is surface capture.
